quotes.text: Mountain climbers are like a moving plank: You start in a raised push-up position and hop your feet forward, one at a time, toward your chest.
quotes.closest: Mountain climbers are like a moving plank: You start in a raised push-up position and hop your feet forward, one at a time, toward your chest.

quotes.text: Start on your hands and knees with your arms straight and hands placed directly under your shoulders.
quotes.closest: Start on your hands and knees with your arms straight and hands placed directly under your shoulders.

quotes.text: Extend your legs back behind you, supporting your body on your hands and toes. Your body should form a straight line from the back of your head to your heels (like a regular, raised push-up position or plank).
quotes.closest: Extend your legs back behind you, supporting your body on your hands and toes. Your body should form a straight line from the back of your head to your heels (like a regular, raised push-up position or plank).

quotes.text: From here, hop one foot toward your chest, and then quickly switch legs, as if you’re running. Try not to let your hips hike up as you move.
Maintain that plank position as you continue to alternate legs.
quotes.closest: Maintain that plank position as you continue to alternate legs.

quotes.text: Weight shifting backward. Shifting your weight backward can reduce some of the pressure on your arms and core, but it can also make it tougher to maintain balance and stability.
quotes.closest: Weight shifting backward. Shifting your weight backward can reduce some of the pressure on your arms and core, but it can also make it tougher to maintain balance and stability.

quotes.text: A helpful adjustment here is to keep your shoulders directly over your wrists and imagine pressing slightly forward.
quotes.closest: A helpful adjustment here is to keep your shoulders directly over your wrists and imagine pressing slightly forward.

quotes.text: Bouncing on your toes. Some people find themselves bouncing on their toes as they drive their knees forward. This can add extra impact, especially for beginners, which might make it harder to keep the movement controlled.
quotes.closest: Bouncing on your toes. Some people find themselves bouncing on their toes as they drive their knees forward. This can add extra impact, especially for beginners, which might make it harder to keep the movement controlled.

quotes.text: To adjust, focus on moving with smooth, intentional steps, almost as if you’re gliding your knees forward rather than bouncing.
quotes.closest: To adjust, focus on moving with smooth, intentional steps, almost as if you’re gliding your knees forward rather than bouncing.

quotes.text: Some rounding in your back is natural, especially as you start to fatigue. If you feel your back rounding excessively, try focusing on drawing your shoulders down and back, which supports a neutral spine position.
quotes.closest: Some rounding in your back is natural, especially as you start to fatigue. If you feel your back rounding excessively, try focusing on drawing your shoulders down and back, which supports a neutral spine position.

quotes.text: Engaging your core helps to keep your torso steady, which can help you feel stronger and less strained throughout the movement.
quotes.closest: Engaging your core helps to keep your torso steady, which can help you feel stronger and less strained throughout the movement.

quotes.text: Step, instead of jump. Rather than jumping to switch legs, step one foot forward, then step it back, and repeat with the other leg.
quotes.closest: Step, instead of jump. Rather than jumping to switch legs, step one foot forward, then step it back, and repeat with the other leg.

quotes.text: Place your hands on an elevated surface, like a sturdy bench or step. This reduces the load on your arms and core, making the exercise less intense than starting from the floor.
quotes.closest: Place your hands on an elevated surface, like a sturdy bench or step. This reduces the load on your arms and core, making the exercise less intense than starting from the floor.

quotes.text: Instead of bringing your knee all the way to your chest, only bring it halfway or as far as is comfortable.
quotes.closest: Instead of bringing your knee all the way to your chest, only bring it halfway or as far as is comfortable.

quotes.text: Pick up the pace. Do the movement at a faster pace to increase the cardio intensity. This will also challenge your core and legs to move quickly and efficiently.
quotes.closest: Pick up the pace. Do the movement at a faster pace to increase the cardio intensity. This will also challenge your core and legs to move quickly and efficiently.

quotes.text: As you do each rep, you might feel your core, shoulder, and arm muscles working, as well as your butt, thighs, and hips.
quotes.closest: As you do each rep, you might feel your core, shoulder, and arm muscles working, as well as your butt, thighs, and hips.

quotes.text: Hip flexors. These muscles help you flex at the hip (thus the name) when you walk and do other activities that require lifting your legs.
quotes.closest: Hip flexors. These muscles help you flex at the hip (thus the name) when you walk and do other activities that require lifting your legs.

quotes.text: Rectus abdominis. This sheet of muscle — often called the "six-pack" muscle — spans the front of your abdomen

quotes.text: Many exercise disciplines incorporate upper extremity weight-bearing exercises in an extended wrist posture, for example push-ups, plank position, and various yoga and Pilates poses.
quotes.closest: Many exercise disciplines incorporate upper extremity weight-bearing exercises in an extended wrist posture, for example push-ups, plank position, and various yoga and Pilates poses.

quotes.text: Mountain climbers are usually programmed by time rather than reps. Beginners should start with 2 to 3 sets of 15 seconds of work and 15 seconds of rest, which totals about 1 to 2 minutes.
quotes.closest: Mountain climbers are usually programmed by time rather than reps. Beginners should start with 2 to 3 sets of 15 seconds of work and 15 seconds of rest, which totals about 1 to 2 minutes.

quotes.text: At intermediate level, use 3 to 4 sets of 20 seconds on and 20 seconds off, and if you are well conditioned, 4 to 5 sets of 30 seconds on and 30 seconds off.
quotes.closest: At intermediate level, use 3 to 4 sets of 20 seconds on and 20 seconds off, and if you are well conditioned, 4 to 5 sets of 30 seconds on and 30 seconds off.

quotes.text: As part of an overall program focusing on muscular strength and conditioning, complete 2–3 sets of 10–15 slow and controlled repetitions.
quotes.closest: As part of an overall program focusing on muscular strength and conditioning, complete 2–3 sets of 10–15 slow and controlled repetitions.

quotes.text: As part of a cardiovascular program with a HIIT focus, complete 6–8 rounds of fast mountain climbers for 20 seconds, with a 10-second rest in between.
quotes.closest: As part of a cardiovascular program with a HIIT focus, complete 6–8 rounds of fast mountain climbers for 20 seconds, with a 10-second rest in between.

quotes.text: They can also be performed at a slow, controlled tempo, which is better for beginners.
quotes.closest: They can also be performed at a slow, controlled tempo, which is better for beginners.

quotes.text: Progress by extending the interval before adding sets, and end the set as soon as your hips start bouncing rather than pushing to the clock.
quotes.closest: Progress by extending the interval before adding sets, and end the set as soon as your hips start bouncing rather than pushing to the clock.

quotes.text: As for challenges with technique, it’s common for the hips to come up too high during mountain climbers, creating a triangle or Downward Dog shape.
Letting your hips pike up. If your backside rises toward the ceiling, you have made the plank easier and taken the core out of the exercise. Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Drive one knee in. Lift your right foot off the ground and bring that knee toward your chest, keeping your hips level rather than letting them rise.
Holding your breath. Very common on this one and it kills your endurance. Find a rhythm and keep breathing through the whole interval.
Breathe. Find a consistent breathing rhythm rather than holding your breath, which is what most women do the first few times they try this.

Slow down. I know that sounds backwards on an exercise built for speed, but almost every woman I watch do these goes fast enough that her hips start bouncing up and down and the core stops working entirely.
Set a pace where your hips stay completely level and your back stays flat, then hold that pace for the whole interval.
Going faster than you can hold. Speed is not the goal, sustained position under speed is. If your hips are bouncing, you are past your pace.
Hands drifting forward. Your hands belong directly under your shoulders. When they creep out in front, your shoulders take on far more load than they should.
Letting your hips sag. The opposite problem drops the load into your lower back. Squeeze your glutes and brace before you start moving your legs.
Alternatively, sometimes your hips may drop too low, creating an excessive arch in your lower back.
If your wrists bother you, elevate your hands on a bench or use dumbbells to keep the wrists neutral.
This option puts less weight on your wrists and upper body, which is useful if you’re looking to build strength gradually in these areas or need to consider an injury.
This decreases the amount of extension in your wrists compared with having your hands flat on the floor. It may feel more comfortable if you experience issues with your fingers or wrists.
stop or cut down activities that are causing the pain – for example, typing, using vibrating tools for work, or playing an instrument
